notes: Single series loop (RLC driven by an AC source), all 7 components in-frame. Net map: 0 = the bottom rail -- one lightly-drawn but continuous run (verified at 6x; it only looks dashed because the light pencil broke up under binarisation) from the lower lead of V-AC 5 at the left corner (122,307) rightwards to the lower lead of Resistor 1 at (412,320), with the GND 6 stem dropping to the ground bars at (272,313); n1 = left corner (130,184): upper lead of V-AC 5 up the left column and right into the left end of Resistor 0 (5 kohm); n2 = Resistor 0 right end to Inductor 2 (10 mH) left lead; n3 = Inductor 2 right lead to Resistor 3 (10 kohm) left end; n4 = Resistor 3 right end to the left plate of Capacitor 4 (5 nF); n5 = right plate of Capacitor 4 -> top-right corner (415,202) -> down the right column to the upper lead of Resistor 1 (10 kohm). Judgment calls: (a) the top rail was traced at 7x and is a plain series chain R0 -> L2 -> R3 -> C4 with no taps or crossings; the left and right columns were traced at 8x and each contains exactly one series element (V-AC 5 on the left, Resistor 1 on the right); (b) the bottom rail's broken appearance is a rendering artefact of light pencil, not a real break -- the fragments are collinear along a single slightly-sloping line and there is no hop or gap in the surrounding geometry, and reading it as broken would leave the source with no return path; (c) the GND 6 stem meets the bottom rail as a plain T at (272,313), so the whole bottom rail is net '0'; (d) the long straight diagonals at the far left (x~8-12), across the upper right ((240,140) to (505,163)) and across the lower left are page-border / ruled lines -- they touch no symbol and are ignored; (e) all 7 bbox centres are inside the 512x512 frame -- no off-frame components; (f) V-AC 5 carries no polarity marks, so its terminal order is arbitrary; index0 is taken as the upper lead. Other 2-terminal parts use index0 = left (horizontal) or top (vertical) as drawn. Order affects no metric.
